subject: biology
title: 1 Ecological Importance a. Bog succession
source: 3. Reduced-Biology grade 11 ck4uozj — 1 Ecological Importance a. Bog succession, pages 132-132 [3. Reduced-Biology_grade_11_ck4uozj.pdf]
textbookText: The mosses play an important role in bog succession from water to climax forest. The bryophytes especially Sphagnum plants along with other hydrophytes form a dense surface covering over the water below. This covering gives the appearance of the soil from the surface. These areas are known as quacking bogs. Later on these bogs are converted into swamps. Ultimately these swamps are replaced by the forest growth. b. Formation of soil: Mosses along with lichens are supposed to be pioneers over the bare rocky surface. They grow on rocks and add organic matter to the substratum after their death that makes the rocks suitable for the growth of higher plants. c. Food and shelter: Numerous invertebrates eat bryophytes, lay their eggs on them or shelter in them. They form a vital part of the construction material of the nest of some birds. d. Soil conservation: Mosses grow in dense mats over the soil surface. They bind the soil particles and prevent soil erosion by running water. e. Pollution: The bryophytes are very sensitive to air pollution. Both alive and air dried mosses can absorb metals. The accumulation of heavy metal in mosses enables them to be used as atmospheric and aquatic pollution indicators.

2. Medicinal uses: The bryophytes contain numerous potentially useful compounds so they help to cure ringworms, ash of moss is mixed with honey and fat to treat cuts, burn and wounds. Liverworts are used for liver disease. Certain bryophytes are also used to obtain a number of antibiotic substances. Sphagnum is used in antiseptic absorbent bandage.
3. Packing material: Most of the mosses are used as packing material after being dried. They make a fairy good packing material in the case of glass ware and other fragile goods.

4. A source of fuel: The hardened and compact dark coloured rich in carbon formed by compression of dead remains of moss (Sphagnum species) accumulated year after year is called peat. These peats are dried, cut into pieces and used as fuel.
5. In experimental Botany: The liverworts and mosses have played an important role as research tools in the various field of Botany such as genetics, experimental morphology and physiology.
6. Ornamental value: Bryophytes have been used for green house crops, potted ornamental plants and in garden soil.
7. Industrial Uses: Mosses are used to make carpets; peats are used to obtain alcohol, ammonium sulphate, paraffin, brown dye, tanning materials, etc.
